newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended Wednesday down, but markets broadly welcomed Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's first budget for seeking to reign in spending and easing foreign exchange controls, dealers said.

The day began with most dealers on tenterhooks ahead of the budget speech. In the immediate aftermath of Manuel's presentation stocks ticked up across the board, but the reaction was seen as a knee-jerk response.
With the all-share index nearing all-time high levels and a recent strong run on industrials, some profit-taking entered the market later.
"There was probably a touch of profit-taking. People had expected a positive budget and that was what we got so some guys may have cashed in," one dealer said.
The industrials index lost 16.1 points to 8,368.6, but the all-share provded more resilient and ended the day up 6.1 points to 7,168.1.
The picture among blue-chips was mixed with Richemont losing 200 cents to 59.50 rand, while De Beers gained 50 cents to 161.00 rand and Johnnic adds 50 cents 58.75 rand.
Manuel's speech was dominated by the announcement of measures to relax remaining exchange controls on South African nationals and residents.

Individuals will be allowed to invest a limited amount directly abroad or alternatively hold foreign currency deposits with South African banks. South African nationals and residents will for the first time be free to keep funds earned abroad outside the country.
Companies will also be given increased freedom to invest overseas and will be able to raise foreign funding on the strength of their South Africa balance sheet.

Manuel also delivered on a long-standing promise to narrow the gap between state income and expenditure when he estimated the budget deficit in the year to March 31, 1998, at 24.7 billion rand or four percent of gross domestic product, down from 5.1 percent.
Economists across the board welcomed the budget.
"I think the moves on exchange controls are long overdue, but very positive. It is what everyone has been looking for," said Henry Flint, economist at stockbroker Mathison and Hollidge.
"I think from now on we can expect exchange controls to be removed more rapidly."
The golds index continued its recent firmer trend and gained support from positive sentiment stemming from the budget as well as a steadying bullion price.
The golds index added 6.1 points to 1,447.5.

In futures early gains on strong institutional buying were built on as the budget speech was delivered, but the proximity of the contract close-out date on Monday lead to a mixed performance at the close of trade.
The all-share March contract rose to 6,507/20 from 6,496 as the industrials contract stood at 8,016/25 from 8,034. The golds contract was at 1,000/1,010 from 1006.
